questions.category: A. PERFORMS COMMON OCCUPATIONAL SKILLS — 16 / Task 1. Performs safety-related functions — 2
questions.question: Before changing knives on a jointer, what is the safest first step?
questions.explanation: Lockout prevents accidental startup. Machine guards and adjustments are not enough without isolating energy.

questions.category: A. PERFORMS COMMON OCCUPATIONAL SKILLS — 16 / Task 2. Maintains tools and equipment — 4
questions.question: A table saw begins burning hardwood during rip cuts. What should be checked first?
questions.explanation: Burning usually comes from friction. Dull blades or misalignment can pinch the stock.

questions.category: A. PERFORMS COMMON OCCUPATIONAL SKILLS — 16 / Task 3. Organizes work — 4
questions.question: What is the purpose of a cut list?
options: To organize part sizes, quantities, and materials
questions.explanation: A cut list helps plan material use and machining. It reduces waste and missing parts.

questions.category: A. PERFORMS COMMON OCCUPATIONAL SKILLS — 16 / Task 4. Performs routine work practices — 4
questions.question: Why should veneered panels be stored flat and protected?
options: To prevent warping and surface damage
questions.explanation: Veneer faces damage easily. Poor storage can warp panels or scratch finished surfaces.

questions.category: A. PERFORMS COMMON OCCUPATIONAL SKILLS — 16 / Task 5. Uses communication and mentoring techniques — 2
questions.question: A drawing detail is unclear. What should a cabinetmaker do?
questions.explanation: Clarifying prevents costly mistakes. Communication is part of professional workmanship.
